subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs support default delete-after-run cleanup, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR defaults recurring isolated jobs to cleanup, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 proposes rejecting the same state; automation cannot safely choose the permanent cron contract.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted omitted-job handling and reconciliation with the strict-validation PR before merge.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its caller and upgrade issues are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration, accepting that this PR does not fully close the linked bug.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted omitted-job handling and reconciliation with the strict-validation PR before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main cron normalization and store history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the lifecycle contract choice.
